## Excursions to Raqchi: the Temple of Viracocha between Cusco and Puno

[Raqchi](/peru/place/raqchi/) lies in the southern part of Peru's Cusco Region, in the Vilcanota River valley. Visitors come to see the remains of a large Inca temple complex, its stone and adobe architecture, storage buildings, and the layout of an ancient settlement.

We include Raqchi on journeys **between Cusco and Puno**. It is a convenient way to turn a long drive through the Andes into a day punctuated by historical stops. We do not currently offer a separately priced excursion devoted only to Raqchi, so you should consider the complete product, its direction, and the length of the stop.

## What remains at the archaeological complex

The main attraction is the Temple of Viracocha. Its tall wall, with a stone foundation and adobe upper section, gives an impression of the original structure's scale. According to the Cusco Directorate of Culture, the surviving wall reaches approximately 14 meters and the original rectangular building was about 92 meters long.

Nearby stand the remains of other buildings and large groups of circular storage rooms, commonly called *qollqas*. They recall the complex's economic function: storing food and materials was essential to supplying the vast Inca state.

During your visit, notice the combination of building materials, the arrangement of structures around courtyards, and the settlement's relationship with the river valley. The walls are protected archaeological monuments; climbing on them or leaving inscriptions is forbidden.

## Cusco to Puno: a sightseeing coach stop at Raqchi

On the [“Cusco to Puno: Andahuaylillas, Raqchi and La Raya” excursion](/peru/cusco/cusco-puno-andes-bus/), travelers leave Cusco and encounter several periods of Andean history along the way. Andahuaylillas offers a church with colonial decoration; Raqchi introduces Inca monuments. The route then continues through Sicuani, the high-altitude La Raya Pass, and Pucará to Puno.

The advantage of this format is a sequence of historically varied stops within a single day. Raqchi becomes part of a broader account of the region, but time at the site is limited by the overall transfer schedule. If detailed archaeological exploration is your priority, discuss whether extra time can be allocated in advance.

A similar itinerary with many of the same stops, but **in the reverse direction**, is [“Puno to Cusco: sightseeing coach through the Andes”](/peru/puno-and-lake-titicaca/puno-cusco-andes-tourist-bus/). Here Raqchi is visited on the way from the Titicaca region to Cusco. Choose according to the actual order of cities in your journey.

## Belmond Andean Explorer: Raqchi on a train journey

Another option is the [Belmond Andean Explorer from Cusco to Lake Titicaca](/peru/cusco/belmond-andean-explorer-cusco-titicaca/). Our itinerary includes a sightseeing stop at Raqchi. The train then continues through mountain areas toward the lake, with accommodation and the overnight stay on board.

This is a different travel experience from a tourist coach. A rail journey involves extended time aboard the train and its own service and stop schedule. The sights included on a coach excursion cannot automatically be assumed to be part of the train itinerary.

Raqchi is also near the road connecting the two cities. Simply passing through the area without stopping to visit the archaeological complex is an entirely different experience.

## Raqchi or other stops on the route: what to choose

| Place | Why it is interesting |
|---|---|
| Raqchi | Inca architecture |
| Andahuaylillas | Colonial church |
| La Raya | Mountain landscapes |
| Pucará | Pre-Inca culture |

Both coach routes combine these stops, but the arrangements are set out in the respective [Cusco departure itinerary](/peru/cusco/cusco-puno-andes-bus/) or [Puno departure itinerary](/peru/puno-and-lake-titicaca/puno-cusco-andes-tourist-bus/). Buying a ticket for a different mode of transport does not entitle you to the same set of excursions.

It is worth reading about the [Raqchi archaeological complex](/peru/place/raqchi/) in advance. Understanding the site helps you see which parts are especially significant and why the visit offers more than a quick photo stop.

## Altitude, travel, and visiting conditions

Raqchi is approximately 3,480 meters above sea level. Even though the site is relatively flat, the sun, dry air, and altitude can make walking tiring. Bring water, a hat, sunscreen, and wind-protective clothing.

The Cusco Directorate of Culture publishes rules for protecting the archaeological park. Visitors must not climb ancient walls, damage structures, or fly drones without permission. Check access rules and opening hours before departure, as they can change and the sightseeing coach follows its own timetable.

On a longer trip through [Peru](/peru/), Raqchi fits especially well into a journey through the Andes toward [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). That way, one transfer introduces both historic buildings and changing mountain scenery.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Raqchi

### Does Ada Tours offer an excursion exclusively to Raqchi?

We offer Raqchi as part of longer routes between Cusco and Puno. Visiting only the complex would require a separately agreed itinerary.

### Can I see Raqchi on the way from Puno to Cusco?

Yes. Our [sightseeing coach from Puno to Cusco](/peru/puno-and-lake-titicaca/puno-cusco-andes-tourist-bus/) stops at the Raqchi complex.

### Is Raqchi included on the Belmond Andean Explorer journey?

Yes. The [published Belmond Andean Explorer itinerary](/peru/cusco/belmond-andean-explorer-cusco-titicaca/) includes a sightseeing stop at Raqchi. This is a separate train journey, not a regular coach ticket.

### What is the most important thing to see at Raqchi?

The Temple of Viracocha, with its high central wall, and the remains of the circular Inca storehouses. The length of the visit depends on the chosen itinerary and its schedule.

## Excursions in the Sacred Valley of the Incas: history, gastronomy, and adventure

The [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) lies along the Urubamba River in the mountainous Cusco Region. Ancient terraces, Inca settlements, and craft traditions coexist with modern life in Andean communities. A day trip offers several perspectives on the region, although the order and selection of stops depend heavily on the excursion.

We offer **cultural sightseeing itineraries**, programs with a gastronomic experience, and **separate adventure activities**. Choose according to your main interest: Inca architecture, textiles and local traditions, Andean cuisine, or outdoor physical activity in the mountains.

## Classic excursion from Cusco

The [“Sacred Valley of the Incas” excursion](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/) includes Urubamba, Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Chinchero, Moray, and Awanakancha, as listed in its program. Archaeological complexes, agricultural terraces, and craft traditions bring the valley's history to life. The itinerary also includes lunch at a restaurant serving national cuisine.

A separate option is [“Sacred Valley: Pisac, Awanakancha and Ollantaytambo”](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-pisac-awanakancha-ollantaytambo/). This full-day excursion from Cusco includes the Pisac craft market, Awanakancha center with llamas and alpacas, the Ollantaytambo complex, and lunch as specified. Its list of stops is narrower than that of the first excursion: **Moray and Chinchero are not automatically included**.

When choosing between these trips, decide whether you want to cover more places in one day or spend more time exploring particular parts of the valley.

## Pisac and Ollantaytambo: architecture and living culture

Pisac is known for its archaeological terraces, handicrafts, and valley views. Ollantaytambo is distinguished by monumental stone structures and the preserved layout of its old settlement. Both appear on several excursions, but each program allows different amounts of time and offers different additional activities.

Awanakancha is particularly relevant for travelers interested in wool products. The [excursion through Pisac and Awanakancha](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-pisac-awanakancha-ollantaytambo/) includes an introduction to Andean animals and fiber processing. This is a feature of that particular tour, not a mandatory element of every journey through the valley.

## Moray, Maras, and a gastronomic day

Moray is famous for a system of concentric earthen terraces arranged at different elevations, often linked to Inca agricultural experiments. Maras, by contrast, is known for networks of small salt pools on a mountainside. The attractions complement each other, but they are physically separate places.

To visit both, we offer the [“Moray, Maras Salt Terraces and Lunch at MIL Centro” excursion](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/moray-maras-mil-centro-lunch/). The itinerary pairs the two sites with a tasting lunch at MIL Centro, where contemporary cuisine draws on Andean ingredients.

Another gastronomic combination is [“Pisac, Ollantaytambo and Lunch with a Show at Wayra”](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/pisac-ollantaytambo-wayra-lunch/). Its historical section covers Pisac and Ollantaytambo, followed by lunch at Wayra with traditional dancing and a Peruvian Paso horse performance.

**MIL Centro and Wayra are different restaurants and distinct excursion experiences.** Lunch at one must not be promised when booking the other program. Meal arrangements, transportation, and access to the specific sites should be checked in the chosen excursion's description.

## Via ferrata and ziplining: an active Sacred Valley

Alongside cultural excursions, we offer stand-alone outdoor activities. The [Sacred Valley via ferrata](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-via-ferrata/) follows a rock face equipped with metal ladders and fixed safety anchors. Its description includes an approximately 300-meter-high rock route and a roped descent with safety equipment. Prior climbing experience is not listed as mandatory, but participants must check the physical demands and medical restrictions before joining.

[Ziplining in the Sacred Valley](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/) is a different activity. The course uses six cables of varying lengths, totaling about 2 km, and a safety harness. It suits travelers who want to experience speed above mountain scenery, but **it does not replace an archaeological sightseeing excursion**.

Each activity should be arranged separately, including restrictions based on age, weight, and health, actual transfers, and footwear requirements. The presence of an adventure site in the valley does not mean it is included in a classic sightseeing itinerary.

## Choosing an excursion in the Sacred Valley

| Travel goal | Option |
|---|---|
| Archaeology and crafts | Pisac, Ollantaytambo |
| Terraces and salt | Moray, Maras |
| Creative cuisine | Lunch at MIL Centro |
| Traditional show | Lunch at Wayra |
| Rock-face ascent | Via ferrata |
| Cable descent | Zipline |

To explore the valley's history, begin with the [cultural excursion from Cusco](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/). If mountain gastronomy and local ingredients interest you, compare [MIL Centro](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/moray-maras-mil-centro-lunch/) and [Wayra](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/pisac-ollantaytambo-wayra-lunch/). For an active day, choose the [via ferrata](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-via-ferrata/) or [zipline](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/), with the appropriate preparation.

## Altitude, transfers, and preparation

The Sacred Valley lies in the Andes, and elevations vary between settlements and visitor sites. Day excursions involve travel between stops. Water, strong sun protection, comfortable shoes, and light warm clothing are helpful even on vehicle-based excursions.

When planning, consider how much time remains for Pisac or Ollantaytambo after the transfers. Moray and Maras can require additional logistics. Outdoor sports need their own time allocation and assessment of physical demands.

If your journey centers on ancient cities, explore [cultural and historical travel](/interests/culture-and-history/). For itineraries with physical challenges, see the [adventure](/interests/adventure/) theme. The specific inclusions are stated in each excursion's itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about Sacred Valley excursions

### Can I visit Pisac and Ollantaytambo in one day?

Yes. Both are included in several published Ada Tours excursions, including the [full-day itinerary from Cusco](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-pisac-awanakancha-ollantaytambo/).

### Are Moray and Maras the same place?

No. Moray is known for circular terraces, while Maras is famous for salt pools. Both are included on a [separate excursion with lunch at MIL Centro](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/moray-maras-mil-centro-lunch/).

### Is ziplining included in a general Sacred Valley tour?

There is no basis to consider it part of the cultural sightseeing routes. [Ziplining](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/) is offered as a separate activity with its own participation requirements.

### Are there excursions with a gastronomic program?

Yes. The catalog separately lists lunch at [MIL Centro](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/moray-maras-mil-centro-lunch/) and lunch with a show at [Wayra](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/pisac-ollantaytambo-wayra-lunch/). Each itinerary has its own set of historical stops.

## Moray, Maras Salt Terraces and MIL Centro: one day in the Sacred Valley

**This excursion connects 2 famous sites in the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) with lunch at the MIL Centro gastronomic project.** At [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), you will see unusual concentric terraces; at [Maras](/peru/place/maras/), mountainside salt pools. The day concludes with tasting cuisine inspired by the Andes' ingredients and traditions.

Our excursion includes all three stops. Together, they show how agriculture, history, and contemporary approaches to researching local food are interwoven within one region. There is a meaningful connection between the archaeological sites and the meal, making the experience more than a series of photo stops.

Departure time, transport, guide language, and the final price are agreed for your travel date. These details matter particularly because lunch at MIL Centro follows a set schedule.

## Moray: why did the Incas build circular terraces?

[Moray](/peru/place/moray/) is known for several sunken circular structures lined with stone terraces. From above, they resemble giant concentric rings set among Andean hills. Sunlight and temperature vary between levels, giving rise to a widespread academic hypothesis that the site was used for agricultural experiments.

Calling it an “Inca agricultural research station” sounds convincing, but the complex's exact construction and purpose remain subjects of research. It is more accurate to describe the terraces as linked to agriculture and the study of growing conditions while acknowledging uncertainty about their precise historical role.

At Moray, pay attention to the geometry of the structures and their position in the mountain landscape. Their arrangement is particularly clear from viewpoints where several terrace levels can be seen together. Current monument regulations determine access to individual sections and paths.

## Maras: how mountain salt pools work

The [Maras Salt Terraces](/peru/place/maras/) look entirely different. Numerous small pools dot a hillside, where salty water slowly evaporates. Shades of white, ochre, and pale pink form a striking pattern against the dry mountain slopes.

Here, you can follow the practical process of local salt production: water is channeled into individual basins, then salt remains after evaporation. This is an ongoing economic activity, so visitors must respect walking restrictions and stay out of working pools.

**Moray and Maras complement each other.** Moray focuses on archaeology and circular agricultural terraces; Maras brings together salt, water, landscape, and the modern lives of local producers. The combination tells a fuller story of the resources and work of the highland valley.

| Stop | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Moray | Circular terraces and agricultural history |
| Maras | Mountain salt pools |
| MIL Centro | Andean tasting cuisine |

## Lunch at MIL Centro: local ingredients explored through taste

MIL Centro is located near the Moray archaeological complex at approximately **3,568 meters above sea level**, according to the restaurant's official information. This gastronomic project connects cuisine, the natural environment, and research into local biodiversity. Its creators include chefs Virgilio Martínez and Pía León, as well as Malena Martínez, who leads the Mater research initiative.

The menu uses ingredients associated with high-altitude ecosystems and seasonal Andean agriculture. MIL Centro's official website describes an eight-course tasting menu whose composition changes with the seasons. This gives a useful idea of the dining format, but the exact menu and meal included in your trip must follow the confirmed reservation.

Our excursion **includes a tasting lunch at MIL Centro**. The specific dishes, drinks, dietary restrictions, and additional services are confirmed at booking. Notify us of allergies and dietary preferences in advance, and agree any available menu adaptations before the visit is confirmed.

For food enthusiasts, the restaurant is itself a reason to visit the Sacred Valley. Travelers whose main interest is food and local ingredients can also explore [Ada Tours' food and wine itineraries](/interests/food-and-wine/). Other historical and cultural experiences are collected under [culture and history](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Altitude, travel, and the day's pace

Moray, Maras, and MIL Centro are in the highland part of Cusco Region. At MIL Centro, the altitude exceeds 3,500 meters. Even people who walk comfortably at sea level may experience discomfort from a rapid gain in altitude. Allow time to adjust to the Andes and assess how you feel, especially during the first days after arrival.

Bring sunglasses, sunscreen, water, several clothing layers, and comfortable shoes. Mountain weather can change quickly, and temperatures on exposed ground may feel very different from those inside the restaurant.

MIL Centro's operating schedule also affects the choice of date. The restaurant has its own seating times, and a tasting lunch occupies a significant part of the day. Agree the sequence and timing of stops beforehand so that the archaeological visits remain substantial and lunch is relaxed.

The excursion is part of the [33-day VIP tour of Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/). Within such a long itinerary, it offers a measured combination of cultural and culinary experiences between longer transfers. Travelers wishing to focus on one region can also consider separate [Peru tours](/peru/tour/), comparing their Sacred Valley days and included activities.

## Frequently asked questions about Moray, Maras and MIL Centro

### Can Moray and Maras be visited on the same trip?

Yes. They are in the same part of the Sacred Valley and are combined in a published Ada Tours excursion. Transfers and the lunch time at MIL Centro should be arranged in advance.

### What exactly does lunch at MIL Centro include?

The program confirms a tasting lunch. The exact courses, drinks, and possibilities for dietary adaptation depend on the agreed reservation. MIL Centro's public description illustrates contemporary Andean cuisine but does not replace the specific booking terms.

### Should I acclimatize before the excursion?

Planning the visit after gradual acclimatization is advisable, especially if you have been at sea level. MIL Centro is about 3,568 meters above sea level; travelers with individual medical risks should discuss a suitable plan with a physician.

### How is Moray different from Maras?

Moray is an archaeological complex with circular agricultural terraces. Maras is known for working salt pools on a mountainside. Together, they illuminate different aspects of Andean history and livelihoods.

## Via ferrata in the Sacred Valley of the Incas: rock climbing and a roped descent

The [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) is known for archaeological monuments, mountain landscapes, and settlements along the Urubamba River. Travelers wishing to add an active experience to a cultural journey can try a **via ferrata**: an equipped route on a rock face with metal footholds and safety cables.

Ada Tours offers the [“Sacred Valley Via Ferrata” excursion](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-via-ferrata/). The route follows a rock face approximately **300 meters** high, with metal ladders, steel anchors, and protection on the climbing sections. It also includes a separate **abseil of approximately 100 meters**. Previous experience in traditional rock climbing is not required.

## How a via ferrata works

The term *via ferrata* refers to a path equipped with iron fixtures over rocky terrain. Participants use fixed rungs, ladders, footholds, and a specialized safety system. Unlike free rock climbing, progressing along the route does not require finding each hold independently on the natural rock.

Nevertheless, **the equipment does not eliminate physical exertion**. The ascent takes place above the valley, may involve narrow sections, and requires confidence when moving at height. Safety carabiners, harnesses, and helmets must be used according to instructors' directions.

Peru's official tourism portal confirms the existence of an equipped via ferrata in the valley and its combination with a roped descent. Age, weight, health, and equipment requirements are set by the chosen operator and must be checked before participating.

## Climbing above the valley: what travelers see

The Sacred Valley lies in the Andes, where mountain slopes meet fields, settlements, and the Urubamba River valley. From above, you can see the contours of the mountainous terrain and green areas along the river. The activity offers an unusual way to experience Peru's geography.

The reference to **approximately 300 meters** describes the rock route, not a guaranteed free-fall distance or the height of every platform. Climbs are supervised by the organizer, and the pace and stops depend on the group's condition and current circumstances.

If you have a strong fear of heights, do not choose the activity solely for a photograph with a mountain view. Discuss the route's actual difficulty, whether a safe early exit is possible, and which sections require independent movement before committing.

## Abseiling: how the descent differs

The excursion includes a **roped descent of around 100 meters**, known as abseiling or rappelling. This involves controlled downward movement on a rock face using safety equipment.

It is a different technique from climbing metal rungs, so a separate briefing, checks of attachments, and understanding how to operate the safety system are essential before descending. Moving equipment or changing the sequence of actions without an instructor's permission is dangerous.

Even first-time participants must follow their guides' instructions and assess their abilities realistically. Confirm precise medical requirements and age limits with the operator.

## Via ferrata or ziplining: 2 different adventures

Ada Tours also offers [“Ziplining in the Sacred Valley”](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/). Both activities take place in the same region, but they work in fundamentally different ways.

| Activity | Main action |
|---|---|
| **Via ferrata** | Climbing a rock face and descending on a rope |
| [Ziplining](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/) | Traveling along cables above the valley |

If you want to **move across the rock face yourself**, the via ferrata is more suitable. Ziplining is for travelers who want to experience gliding through the air along a sequence of cables. The two have separate product descriptions and should not automatically be treated as a combined package.

## Preparing for the via ferrata

On exposed rock, expect possible wind, sun, and sudden weather changes. Choose clothing that allows free movement, closed non-slip shoes, and sun protection. Water is useful before and after the activity; confirm in advance what you may take onto the route.

The experience takes place in a high-altitude region of the Andes. Acclimatization and tolerance of physical exertion matter for some participants. If you have a medical condition or doubts about your ability to participate, seek individualized advice from a physician and the operator before booking.

Other outdoor sports experiences appear under [Adventure](/interests/adventure/). Regular visits to the valley's archaeological sites involve different preparation and do not replace the safety procedures required on the rock face.

## Frequently asked questions about the via ferrata

### Do I need rock-climbing experience?

Previous climbing experience is **not required** for this excursion. A safety briefing, equipment checks, and the ability to move confidently at height are still essential.

### How high is the route?

The program describes a rock face of **approximately 300 meters** and an abseil of around **100 meters**. Exact details of the descent depend on the operator's current route.

### Is ziplining included?

Ziplining is offered as a separate [Ada Tours excursion](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/). Its inclusion in this product is not confirmed.

### Is a price specified?

No fixed price is stated for this excursion. Rates from another company should not be substituted without confirming the terms.

## Sacred Valley via ferrata: which journey offers this activity?

The [via ferrata in the Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-via-ferrata/) suits travelers wishing to add a climb on an equipped rock face to a historical journey through Peru. Participants move along metal ladders and fixed sections using a safety system; the described route follows a rock face approximately 300 meters high and includes a roped descent of about 100 meters. Because this is an active experience at height, your physical condition, comfort with exposed spaces, and available supervision matter.

You can choose this excursion on the [8-day private “Inca Deluxe” journey](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/). The main itinerary covers Lima, Cusco, the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), and Machu Picchu. **The via ferrata is listed as an optional extra**. Participation, pricing, and its place in the day's schedule are arranged separately; the presence of an excursion module in the tour description does not mean it is included in the base price.

## Fitting a climbing route into a busy day

On the “Inca Deluxe” trip, the Sacred Valley sightseeing day combines [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), the terraces of [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), and the salt-producing area of [Maras](/peru/place/maras/). The same stage offers two distinct outdoor sports options: via ferrata and ziplining. Before booking, decide how much time to devote to the archaeological sites and how much to an active experience.

The rock-climbing section places different demands on arms and legs than walking around an archaeological complex. Participants must repeatedly adjust their safety attachments while moving on an exposed slope. If leisurely exploration of historical sites and time for lunch matter more, the sporting addition may require adjusting the order of stops. Time at the activity site, transfers, and compatibility with the rest of the itinerary are agreed individually.

After the flight from Lima to Cusco, the route first heads into the valley; travelers reach Machu Picchu later aboard the Hiram Bingham train. Andean altitude, temperature differences between sun and shade, rain, and how you feel all matter when choosing the activity day. Allow extra time for the briefing and return transfer to the hotel.

## Via ferrata or ziplining: which format to choose

| Option | Main feature |
|---|---|
| Via ferrata | Climbing a rock face with ladders and safety protection |
| Ziplining | Gliding along tensioned cables |

Via ferrata involves navigating vertical sections and moving independently through a sequence of elements. [Sacred Valley ziplining](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/) works differently: participants follow a route of six cables using safety gear. Both provide an unusual view of the landscape, but differ in physical effort, sensation of height, and duration. If you are specifically looking for journeys offering ziplining, see the [separate catalog of these itineraries](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/tour/).

Before choosing, confirm the organizer's rules regarding age, body weight, health, clothing, and footwear. Sports climbing experience is not specified as mandatory for this excursion, but a briefing and individual assessment of suitability remain necessary.

## What to confirm before booking

Check the activity site's operating dates and hours, included safety equipment, language of instruction, advance-reservation requirements, and alternatives in bad weather. Request a separate quote for the additional activity and transfers: optional excursions are excluded from the base inclusions of the source tour itinerary.

For a quieter holiday, you can keep the main [cultural itinerary in Peru](/peru/tour/) without the climbing segment and spend more time at historical sites. If the via ferrata will be one of the main highlights, discuss it while planning the entire sequence of the journey.

## Frequently asked questions about tours with via ferrata

### Is via ferrata already paid for on the “Inca Deluxe” itinerary?

No. It is listed as an additional excursion. Its terms and price must be agreed separately.

### Can I complete the route without climbing experience?

Prior climbing experience is not required for this excursion. Eligibility depends on the briefing, physical condition, and the operator's rules.

### Can I do the via ferrata and visit Moray and Maras on the same day?

That combination can be discussed when arranging the day's program. Listing all stops and options in an itinerary does not mean sufficient time has automatically been allocated for every activity.
